item: R5 / A5 - a transient between two adjacent snapshots
classification: INSTRUMENT ATTESTATION, reported apart from the pre-registered corpus. Nothing here enters A, B or C.
question: is NO_CHANGE_AT_SAMPLED_POINTS a real distinction, or only a renaming of NO_EVENT_IN_HORIZON?

parameters.shiftToleranceUnchanged: the pre-registered value 3 is not altered

rule: a limit of the observing instrument is never the absence of a game event. The declared 12-frame grid gives the same verdict for a real transient and for a byte that never moves, so that verdict may not claim the horizon was empty. The denser grid is what separates them, and it is reported as a diagnostic rather than adopted as the default: more samples cost frames and more observed changes is not success.

git.commitSubject: S11B-R / R4, R5, R6: the indicator was not proof, the label was not a measurement, and the provenance was not a provenance

provenance.reproducibilityNote: every declared source file matched its committed version at run time

groundTruth.why: raised on a press edge and cleared about 3.0 frames later, entirely inside one 12-frame sampling interval. The event is real and caused by the action, and no snapshot of the probe can catch it. The only honest verdict is NO_CHANGE_AT_SAMPLED_POINTS; NO_EVENT_IN_HORIZON would present the sampling density as the absence of a game event. transientWitness counts the firings so a test can prove the event happened rather than assert it.

eventReallyHappened.note: the witness is a separate address outside the probe, so the event is proved rather than assumed

transient.note: no change at the sampled points; a transient entirely between two adjacent snapshots is NOT excluded
